A FILM CREW PRIED AN ACTOR OUT OF A GIANT WORM'S MOUTH, SANK AN AIRPORT, WALKED A RAPTOR ON A LEASH AND SPUN UP A TORNADO. NOT ONE OF THESE SETS WAS EVER BUILT

5.5M views. 39 seconds

it opens on a desert stage in front of a blue screen. a huge worm puppet hangs off a crane, the crew sits at monitors on a dolly track, and when its mouth snaps shut two guys in black tees have to pull it open by hand. then a director with a megaphone calls action on a miniature airport and a jet goes down into a wall of water. then a jungle set where a guy runs from a raptor while two people in blue suits hold it back on ropes. last one, a green screen hall full of giant fans, a fabric funnel on the ceiling, and a tornado tearing through a tiny city with a red car flying out of it

the crew, the sets, the creatures, all of it is AI

why it works:

→ it's behind the scenes, not the movie. you see dolly tracks, monitors, tracking dots on the blue screen. your brain checks the gear and stops checking the monster

→ every set shows how it was "made". crane, ropes, fans, a megaphone. the rig explains the effect so the impossible part feels handled

→ the people do boring set jobs. holding cables, sitting at screens, waiting for the take. that's what real BTS footage looks like

→ four worlds, one production. same studio light, same crew shirts, same handheld camera, so it plays like one shoot day instead of random clips

→ it escalates. a puppet, then a crash, then a live dinosaur, then weather. each set is bigger than the last

the takeaway: if you want AI to look real, show the fake. a visible rig makes people believe the shot

multi-scene sequences that hold one look across 39 seconds are where seedance 2.5 surprises the most, and you can make them inside @Picsart

Anthropic just open-sourced the python SDK behind Claude Code. you can now build your own AI agent with it. 

this official Anthropic project lets developers bring Claude Code’s agent capabilities directly into their Python applications.

it’s called Claude Agent SDK for Python.

and it already has 8.5K+ GitHub stars.

here’s what makes it powerful:

→ build autonomous agents: give Claude tasks and let it use tools, execute commands, read files, edit code, and complete multi-step workflows.

→ use the Claude Code toolset: access tools like Read, Write, Edit, and Bash from your Python application.

→ create custom tools: turn your own Python functions into tools Claude can call whenever it needs them.

→ connect MCP servers: integrate external services and tools, or create in-process MCP servers directly inside your application.

→ control agent behavior: use hooks to intercept tool calls, approve or block actions, and enforce your own rules.

→ manage permissions: decide which tools Claude can use, which actions require approval, and which operations should be blocked.

→ build interactive agents: use ClaudeSDKClient for ongoing conversations, streaming responses, and bidirectional communication.

→ manage agent sessions: continue previous conversations, resume sessions, and configure system prompts and working directories.

here’s how to set it up:

you need Python 3.10 or later.

1. install the SDK:

pip install claude-agent-sdk

1. create a Python file called http://agent.py.
2. add this simple example:

import anyio
from claude_agent_sdk import query
async def main():
    async for message in query(
        prompt="Create a simple Python calculator"
    ):
        print(message)
http://anyio.run(main)

1. run your script:

python http://agent.py

that’s it. you’ve just created a basic Claude-powered coding agent.

a few important things to know:

→ the Claude Code CLI is bundled with the Python package, so you don’t need to install it separately.

→ you can still use a system-wide Claude Code installation or specify a custom CLI path.

→ the SDK is MIT licensed and free to install.

→ you’ll still need access to Claude models, and usage is subject to Anthropic’s pricing and applicable account terms.

→ the Python SDK is designed to run Claude’s agent loop, not just send ordinary chatbot prompts.

if you’re building AI applications with Python, this gives you a powerful starting point for creating agents with real tools and control over their behavior.

save this, and follow for more useful open-source tools.
